message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **federal long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(If you’re targeting a specific province, you’ll want to add that province’s own holidays – e.g., Family Day in Alberta, St. Patricks’ Day in Ontario, etc.)

| Long Weekend | Holiday | Date (2023) | Weekend Days | Notes |
|--------------|---------|-------------|--------------|-------|
| **Family Day** | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick) | **Monday, Feb 20** | Feb 18–20 | Creates a 3‑day weekend in those provinces. |
| **Good Friday** | Good Friday (all provinces) | **Friday, Apr 7** | Apr 7–9 | Friday + weekend. |
| **Victoria Day** | Victoria Day (all provinces) | **Monday, May 22** | May 20–22 | 3‑day weekend. |
| **Labour Day** | Labour Day (all provinces) | **Monday, Sep 4** | Sep 2–4 | 3‑day weekend. |
| **Thanksgiving** | Thanksgiving (all provinces) | **Monday, Oct 9** | Oct 7–9 | 3‑day weekend. |
| **Christmas** | Christmas Day (all provinces) | **Monday, Dec 25** | Dec 23–25 | 3‑day weekend. |

### Quick Summary

- **Feb 18–20** – Family Day (in provinces that observe it)  
- **Apr 7–9** – Good Friday  
- **May 20–22** – Victoria Day  
- **Sep 2–4** – Labour Day  
- **Oct 7–9** – Thanksgiving  
- **Dec 23–25** – Christmas  

These are the only federal holidays that produced a *true* long weekend (i.e., a holiday falling on a weekday with the adjacent weekend).  

If you need the full list of all Canadian holidays (including provincial ones) or want to generate a calendar programmatically, let me know and I can help you pull that data from an API or a public dataset.
